What it is: a Sigstore bundle v0.3 (JSON, 10 132 bytes decompressed, sha256
622ccacf813f80d5ea3fce3dfa04b3775cf7775b6681761582796baf6aad8c8c) in snappy's raw block format - a varint
length, then 64 literal, 37 one-byte-offset copy and 32 two-byte-offset copy elements. The decompressed JSON
holds bytes above 127 (the largest is 226), so a decoder that passes only ASCII would refuse a real bundle.
Its certificate's SAN is https://github.com/cli/cli/.github/workflows/deployment.yml@refs/heads/trunk.

Why it is here: install.sh decompresses the bundle itself (awk over od) so root can verify it with
`gh attestation verify --bundle` and no login. The literal-only streams the tests build exercise one element
kind; this real one exercises the copies. InstallFlows serves it as an archive's attestation and expects the
refusal to name cli/cli's SAN - which the fake gh can only read when the decoder produced the exact JSON.
